about: The game's terms, one rendering per language (the first; any listed is accepted). checks/i18n.mjs requires a term's rendering in a translation wherever the English message uses one of its forms, for terms with check true; a key in except is let off. ja, zh-Hans and zh-TW are proposals from T-2583, not yet reviewed (docs/localization.md); es and de are empty. zh-TW is Taiwan usage.
keep: $ and the money figures' k, M and B
line symbols and line, station and city names the player or the data gave
km, m, mi, ft, mph, km/h

terms.meaning: A journey people want to make between two places, by any means: what demand counts. Never the player's service.
terms.notes: Counted 回 (ja) and 人次 (zh). zh-TW planners say 旅次; 出行 reads plainer.

terms.meaning: A person riding the player's lines; only for what happens on the player's system.
One journey on the player's lines, as a count.
terms.notes: Also a verb (to ride); counts read naturally as 人次.

terms.meaning: People getting on trains at a station, a count per day.
How many trips people want to make, between which places, and how many would take the player's trains.
A service the player runs: trains, buses or boats on a fixed list of stops.
A place on the track where trains stop, with one platform or more.
The part of a station beside the track where riders get on and off.
A station a line calls at (noun).
terms.notes: Also the verb (trains stop, stop running), so not checked.

terms.meaning: The rails the player draws and builds, blueprint or constructed.
Track and stations drawn but not yet constructed or paid for; free to change.
terms.notes: 蓝图 avoided: in other games it means a copy-and-paste template.

terms.meaning: Turn a blueprint into real track, paying for it; once constructed, removing it refunds nothing.
terms.notes: The button is 着工 / 开工 / 動工; constructed is 建設済み / 已建成 / 已完工.

terms.meaning: Constructed: real track or a real station, as against blueprint.
terms.notes: Build (the tab, the tools) is the general word and covers blueprint too: 建設, 建造, 建造.

terms.meaning: What a rider pays for a trip on the player's lines; set by the player per km.
The daily cost of keeping track and stations, whether trains run or not.
The cost of running trains, per train-km and per car-km.
Fares in minus running costs and upkeep, over a day.
The money the player has to spend.
Money borrowed, paid back from the cash.
Minutes between trains on a line.
How many trains a line runs each way in an hour.
terms.notes: 1時間あたり12本, 每小时12班.

terms.meaning: One car of a train; trains are 1 to 16 cars long.
terms.notes: English car also means an automobile (the next term); read the context. Counter: 8両, 8节 (车厢).

terms.meaning: People driving instead of taking a train; demand's other mode.
More riders on a train than its rated load.
Riders on a train as a share of its rated capacity (Average load).
terms.notes: Also loading data (読み込み / 加载 / 載入).

terms.meaning: How many riders or trains something can take: a train's rated load, a track's trains an hour.
Changing from one line to another on a trip.
A walkway the player builds joining two stations, so riders change between them.
Stations joined by passages or a building, treated as one place to change lines.
terms.notes: To settle with the first translation; no fixed word in either language.

terms.meaning: An outline the player draws that joins the stations inside it into one complex.
A place with its own demand: a zone, shown as a city or a stretch of countryside.
Demand's unit of area; the player mostly sees zones as cities.
Trips between cities, as against trips within one.
Trips between home and work or school.
Why a trip is made: work, school, errands, visits and the rest.
The share of trips that go by the player's trains rather than by car.
Urban rail, mostly underground.
terms.notes: metro area means a city region (都市圏, 都市圈, 都會區).

terms.meaning: Bus lines the player runs on roads.
Boat lines the player runs between ports.
A ferry line's stop on the shore.
Track and trains built for high speeds, costing more.
Track raised on columns above the ground.
Track under the ground, bored deep or cut and cover.
Shallow tunnel built by digging down from the street.
A junction where one track crosses another at a different level.
A pair of switches letting trains move between two side-by-side tracks.
Where track branches or tracks meet.
A station upgrade: sidings past the platforms where trains turn back.
A station upgrade: extra track where a train can wait while another passes.
Something bought for a station that raises its capacity or makes it nicer to use.
A line's trains and headways through each period of the day.
One of the five parts of the day schedules and demand are set by.
The score lines earn each hour.
terms.notes: Also the points a track or bus route is drawn through (点).

terms.meaning: A goal met, with a medal.
A game mode with no money limits and no leaderboard.
A stored game, in the browser or as a file; also the verb.
Walking to and from stations, part of a trip.
